candidates.title: Immunogenicity and Safety of SYS6057 in the Participants Aged 18 Years and Above
candidates.study_design: ClinicalTrials.gov study type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: PHASE1; allocation: RANDOMIZED
candidates.outcome_domain: RSV prevention, immunization, protection, safety, policy, or implementation signal
candidates.key_finding: Human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an enveloped, non-segmented, single-stranded negative-sense RNA virus. It is one of the most common pathogens causing acute lower respiratory infection (ALRI) in infants, young children, and older adults worldwide. Vaccination with an RSV vaccine can prevent lower respiratory tract disease caused by RSV infection. We are conducting a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled, Phase I clinical trial to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of SYS6057 (Recombinant Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine (CHO cell)) in individuals aged 18 years and older.

candidates.title: A Clinical Trial of V175 and V175A in Healthy Adults
candidates.study_design: ClinicalTrials.gov study type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: PHASE1; allocation: RANDOMIZED
candidates.outcome_domain: RSV prevention, immunization, protection, safety, policy, or implementation signal
candidates.key_finding:
Researchers are looking for new vaccines to prevent lower respiratory tract infections. A lower respiratory tract infection is an infection in the lower part of the airways and/or the lungs. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), amongst other respiratory viruses, can cause these infections.

This trial will look at the RSV multivalent vaccines V175 and V175A in healthy participants. The goal of the trial is to learn about the safety of V175 and V175A and if participants tolerate them.

candidates.key_finding:
This clinical trial is being done to learn more about how well a vaccine (Arexvy®) for respiratory syncytial virus, also known as RSV, works in people with weakened immune systems. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does 1 or 2 doses of Arexvy work better in people with weakened immune systems?
* What medical problems do participants have after receiving Arexvy?
